title: Republic v. Caguioa
summary: The Supreme Court ruled that reclaimed or foreshore lands belong to the State and are not susceptible of private appropriation. The Regalian Doctrine applies to all lands of the public domain, including those formed by natural accession along bodies of water.
doctrine: Foreshore and submerged lands belong to the State as part of the public domain. They are not registrable and cannot be the subject of private ownership. Reclaimed lands are also owned by the State and may only be disposed of through a law passed by Congress or through the applicable provisions of the Public Land Act.
fullText:
PERLAS-BERNABE, J.:

The issue is whether foreshore and reclaimed lands may be registered under the Torrens system in the name of a private individual.

The Regalian Doctrine provides that all lands of the public domain belong to the State. This includes foreshore lands, submerged lands, and reclaimed lands. These lands are inalienable and cannot be the subject of commerce or private appropriation.

The government, through the proper agencies, has the authority to reclaim lands from bodies of water. However, reclaimed lands remain part of the public domain and may only be disposed of in accordance with law.
